items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Frank Newton, Bull Williams, Mack Walker, Harold "Hoggy" McFerran and Lester Carr felt the same as I had and the result was that we came back to Springfield.

ctx.x: We played one good dance after Thanksgiving and when we came back to our hotel, Lloyd called a meeting in his room. He had not paid us yet and the idea of the meeting was to say that we had enough money to either take us to New York City or back to Springfield. We could go to New York, if it was satisfactory to everyone and try to get a job. The idea appealed to those that had been to New York before: Dickie Wells, Lloyd, Cecil and Don Frye.

I was the first one to speak about not wanting to take the chance. I had plenty of nerve and would go most any place without being asked twice, but I was afraid of going to New York City without a fixed job and knowing no one. Frank Newton, Bull Williams, Mack Walker, Harold "Hoggy" McFerran and Lester Carr felt the same as I had and the result was that we came back to Springfield.

Three weeks later Lloyd received an offer for a tryout at the Savoy Ballroom in New York City which I had been told, was the largest and best negro dance hall in the country. A well known orchestra leader named Fess Williams had been the house band leader since the place had opened. The tryout was to take place the Saturday before Christmas day which came on Sunday and the following Monday, the Saturday before New Year's Eve, New Year's Day and again the following Monday.
